steps.title: Make a task
steps.body: Real one this time — real API call, real row in the database. Just in your own training project, where it can't bother anyone.

steps.title: Write a title that ends
steps.body: Say what will be true when it's finished. Try: "Draft the agenda for the next design review." Not "agenda."

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Create the task. It'll land in the to-do column.

steps.title: Put your name on it
steps.body: Assign yourself. An unassigned task is a wish — somebody has to be answerable for it.

steps.title: Set a priority
steps.body: Medium is the honest default. Save CRITICAL for things that genuinely stop other people working — if everything is critical, the field stops meaning anything.

steps.title: Give it a real date
steps.body: Constellation reminds you before a due date and escalates after one. So put a date you actually believe, or leave it blank — an invented deadline just trains you to ignore reminders.

steps.title: Say what done means
steps.body: Two lines is plenty here. The habit is what matters: write the finish line before you start running at it.

steps.title: Start work on it
steps.body: Close the task and drag your card into In progress. Dragging and changing the status field do exactly the same thing — use whichever is nearer.

steps.title: Leave a comment
steps.body: Open the task again and post anything. On a real task this is where the questions go — and where they stay findable, attached to the work instead of buried in a channel.

steps.title: Log some time
steps.body: Log half an hour. Anything over two hours in one entry goes to an officer for approval — that gate is what keeps the XP ledger worth trusting.

steps.title: Finish it
steps.body: Drag it to Done. On a real project this is the moment XP is queued for you — here it's suppressed, because practice work shouldn't pay.

steps.title: That's the whole loop
steps.body: Create, own, date, specify, start, discuss, log, finish. Every piece of work in this club goes through those eight steps, and you've now done all of them.
